description.description: Single guidance file for Claude Code; documents the composition-host shape so an agent searches modules/ rather than app/.
Agent-facing environment instructions; identical lerd + Laravel Boost body shared with the Copilot, Junie and Gemini files.
Plans the flip to module-repo-first; every decision links to the issue holding its reasoning. The document plans and changes nothing.
Records where the fleet stands against code-level standards; fixes nothing so each finding stays a separate decision taken with the measurement in hand.

app/ holds exactly five files; search, theming, localization, settings, roles and observability live in 40 liberu-module packages and 4 liberu-theme packages. Before assuming a class lives in app/, search modules/.
Declares provider class, capabilities, required packages and capabilities, default_enabled and Filament plugins — the single source of truth for enablement.
First entry in bootstrap/providers.php so discovery runs before anything depends on it.
Validates constraints with Semver and returns providers in dependency order; disabling a required module raises DependencyResolutionFailed rather than quietly omitting it.
No package declares extra.laravel.providers, so Laravel auto-discovery registers nothing and enablement stays an explicit, separate decision. An architecture rule asserts this stays true.

True for 37 of 40; false for analytics-google, analytics-meta and localization-mymemory, which need third-party credentials so ship installed but off. Adding a module to a composition is therefore installing it — there is no second list to remember.
Holds only MODULES_ENABLED and MODULES_DISABLED, both empty; disabled beats both. Config stays list-free so it cannot become a second source of truth that drifts.
Instantiates only the plugins of enabled modules, rejecting duplicate ids and non-Plugin types — the runtime guard that always fires before any static rule could.
Maps a theme's colors.primary to a Filament palette (unknown → Amber); panel composition is a host concern, so it moved to app/ when foundation-filament dissolved.
Default panel at /admin, tenant-scoped to the Team model with Shield's SyncShieldTenant as persistent tenant middleware.
Panel at /app, deliberately not tenant-scoped and open to any authenticated user.
Both append SetLocale and SecurityHeaders to ->middleware([]) because Filament panels do not run the web group.

Implements seven contracts from four packages; role checks query the pivot team-agnostically because Spatie's hasRole() is bound to an active team context that is unset when canAccessPanel() or the Telescope/Pulse gates run.

A Resource whose model has no team() relationship must override isScopedToTenant(); shield:generate must run inside a team context; filament-shield tenant_model and permission models.team are deliberately null.
permission.teams => true, so roles carry a team_id and Spatie already isolates roles by team — which is why the authorization presentation module disables Shield's tenant resource scoping.
Holds 8 whole-graph rules only; a rule a package can check about itself belongs in the testbench, because a host rule could only ever fail in the host, which is not where the fault is.

Plugin-id uniqueness and renamed-package rules were dropped because ModulePlugins and ModuleValidationGuard reject those conditions first; each was mutation-tested and the failure came from the runtime guard, not the rule.

Owns PackageTestCase, PackageRoot, three shipped Boundary suites and the shared TestUser, plus Pint and PHPStan and their configs — so a new boundary rule is one testbench release rather than a 44-repository sweep.
Each package carries require-dev, its own phpunit.xml and a thin caller of the reusable workflows; a test belongs in a package only if it needs nothing from the host.

Git does not track an empty directory, so a package with no tests of its own published without tests/ at all and Pest aborted with 'The test directory [tests] does not exist'. 34 packages shipped that way once.

Loads the base users migration and brings RefreshDatabase; it implements none of the fleet's actor contracts because doing so would make the testbench require Horizon, Pulse, Telescope, Jetstream, Socialite and Socialstream in all 44 dev trees.

Clones, runs, commits and pushes across the package repositories but deliberately stops short of tagging: a push is recoverable, a tag is what Packagist publishes and what ModuleValidator pins the host to, so an unattended bad wave would be 44 revert-tags.
Rsynced the monorepo into the package repositories — the opposite direction to the flip — and was removed once the coverage-ratchet wave proved a fleet-wide change could ship through fleet alone.
liberusoftware/module-search on GitHub is liberusoftware/search on Packagist.
Compares each manifest against Composer\InstalledVersions, which is why the fleet must keep a version field that composer validate --strict rejects.
Fails the boot with 'Composer package is not installed' before any architecture rule body runs.
base is the shared root and the only theme shipping layouts/app.blade.php, so every public theme renders through the fallback.
Walks the parent chain with a cycle guard.

Merges the tracked themes/ tree with InstalledVersions::getInstalledPackagesByType('liberu-theme'), deduping by realpath so a theme present both ways is one theme; a composition with no themes/ discovers nothing rather than throwing.

vite.config.js reads every themes/*/theme.json and flattens assets.css and assets.js, so installing a theme package is enough to get it built — and a typo in assets fails the build, which is why an architecture rule checks the files exist.
Resolves request param → session → users.locale → Accept-Language → default; precedence request > session > user means a stale session locale can shadow a freshly logged-in user.
Not mounted anywhere yet.
Disabled by default; it require-devs localization-core so its suite can boot a real TranslationProviderRegistry while staying free of the implementation at runtime.
Small type: library packages carrying no manifest, used where an adapter needs implementation independence.
Octane evaluates panel ->colors() once at worker boot, so a colour change needs a worker restart.
resources/js/app.js is empty, there is no Echo client and routes/channels.php holds only Laravel's default channel — treat real-time as an available dependency, not a working feature.
spatie/laravel-permission v8 is blocked by filament-shield ~4.x; spiral/roadrunner-http v4 is blocked by laravel/octane ^2.

A phpstan-level input per repository set from a measured baseline and raised only; unset is -1 rather than 0 because 0 is a real level. The host analyses app/ only, because a package is honest only when analysed against the tree a consumer installs.

PINT.md asks for a pint.json per repository; this deviates because 44 committed copies is how configurations become inconsistent, and Pint has no include mechanism so a shared ruleset is only reachable through --config.
Never in /tmp: WSL's /tmp is wiped on restart and invisible to everyone else, so a handoff written there is lost precisely when the next session needs it.

Coverage <source> is app alone; the Modules and Themes suites were dropped because root autoload-dev maps only Tests\, so they died with 'Class …\Tests\TestCase not found' the moment anything reinstalled.
The independent module repository is source of truth; modules/ becomes Composer output and a change made under modules/ survives only until the next composer update.
A clean install must reproduce modules/ and themes/ byte for byte; a diff means someone edited an installed package instead of its repository, and the next install would silently discard the change.

Every package had diverged from its published repo and the monorepo was the side behind; reconciled in favour of upstream through composer update rather than rsync, because Composer is the mechanism the flip moves toward.

No vendor rename: nothing is republished under a new name, nothing is abandoned, no Packagist vendor permission is needed — and liberu/ was never available, since Packagist protects a vendor once anything publishes under it.
-core is applied only where a sibling provider adapter ships today, not for 'core of the application'; a provider-shaped contract alone is speculative abstraction.
An umbrella presenting three independent modules, which §5.6 forbids; its pieces became sessions-devices-filament, module-manager-filament and the host's ThemeColors.

blog-core, blog-filament, messaging, messaging-api, messaging-filament and search-demo each took their own repository; no foundation package depended on them, which is what made removal a matter of dropping six Composer requires.
Liberu\Foundation\* and Liberu\Themes\* survive because {Domain} reads as the package family; only Authorization → RolesPermissions and the analytics family actually move.
The literal 41-name list plus 3 optional adapters was a second source of truth that could drift.
A rule lives where it can be acted on; a host failure the host cannot fix is a bad rule. The count landed at 8 rather than the planned 6 because two whole-graph additions were kept.
One tests.yml calling all three reusables queued 176 jobs per 44-repository sweep; split into separate files with install and compatibility on tags plus a concurrency group, one sweep is now 44 jobs.

The threshold lives in the package's tests.yml, not phpunit.xml (whose <coverage> element carries no minimum and would be silently ignored) and not a Composer script; two files carrying the same number is two files that can disagree. It ratchets only upward.
Needed plugin-modifies-install-path and filesystem-based collision detection; a per-run in-memory check missed a directory left by a removed package.

Idempotent and takes explicit paths, so it re-runs against checked-out package repositories; it preserves an existing coverage-threshold block, without which one re-run would silently reset every ratchet.

Separate because the second must be re-runnable as coverage grows; a package that lost coverage keeps its old threshold and is reported, because that is a regression to look at rather than a floor to lower.
Do every cross-cutting change while it is still one atomic commit, so the split is last; step 9 is the point of no return.

installed.json freezes psr-4 prefixes and package names until a reinstall, so the monorepo can change what a class does and stay green, but not what it is called — the gate for a rename wave is each package's own suite.
Every case where an exception was available was resolved in favour of a mechanically checkable rule instead.
Holds type => callable so searchAll() names nothing; naming post and group was the actual tie to the demo, and an unregistered type is now absent rather than present and empty.
Exiled: not a documented capability, default-enabled against §12, and its migrations created unprefixed posts and groups tables.

MessageController::users() selected Jetstream's profile_photo_path and had returned a 500 for four releases in any application without Jetstream, invisible because only a Jetstream-carrying host exercised it.
37 findings over 122 audited rule clusters; a rule violated in 400 files is one row with a count, not four hundred rows.

Four ranks describe realized consequence — breaks a consumer, breaks a promise, unenforced, style only. Security is a flag rather than a fifth rank because a supply-chain exposure is risk, and unenforced is already the risk bucket.

Classes are Boundary, CI, Arch, Larastan, Pint and Prose; Prose (per-change) is out of scope because an obligation on the next change has no fleet-wide fact behind it and an audit row for one cannot fail.
Both -livewire packages register a bare global name, which silently loses to any consumer registering the same alias.
21 references across host and reusable workflows; ranked unenforced with a security flag.
A push to liberusoftware/.github changes every repository's CI instantly with no staging.
3 of 216 package files and 0 of 5 host files; a sweep is a fleet-wide semantic change, not a formatting one, and declare_strict_types is not in Pint's laravel preset.
They register a destination only if a transport is bound, and nothing in the fleet or host binds either — so enabling one sends nothing.
Neither CONTEXT.md nor docs/adr/ is present, while CONFORMANCE.md §6 resolves exceptions by pointing at ADRs that have no home.
jetstream-bridge type-hints Illuminate's base User then calls host-only members through traits it neither requires nor declares; a consumer gets a fatal, not a diagnostic.
8 presentation packages; CONFORMANCE.md §6 states 'ADR exceptions: None' while this exception is in force and undocumented.
profiles, search and identity-socialstream all Schema::table('users'); ordering between them is accidental.
18 app()/resolve() call sites and 30 files importing a Facade in domain source; no stock PHPStan rule catches it.
The application composes, modules own behavior, themes own presentation; dependencies flow through declared capabilities and contracts rather than cross-package implementation classes.
Maps the canonical foundation catalog to independently owned packages; product examples are no longer installed here.
Root migrations own only application users and Laravel infrastructure; capability migrations, routes, policies, commands, config, translations and views live with their owning module.
Run in CI and during deployment; a validated module cache must be rebuilt when enabled modules, manifests, lockfiles or environment configuration change.

The deployable host for a property business, combining independently released domain, API, Filament, Livewire and theme packages while keeping tenancy, teams, authentication and composition in one host.
Independent modules with provider-specific transport contracts.
Extends the Liberu default and base themes through the manifest inheritance chain; selected via THEME_DEFAULT/THEME_PUBLIC.
Packagist uses liberusoftware/real-estate-*, the independent GitHub sources use liberusoftware/module-real-estate-*, themes use liberusoftware/theme-*.
Tabbed user form, enriched users table, a read-only view page and three dashboard widgets; backward compatible with no database migrations required.
UserStatsOverview, LatestUsersWidget and UsersByRoleChart.
Podman-based and framework-agnostic: every framework is driven by a YAML definition rather than by lerd hardcoding a framework's name.
site, service, db, env, runtime, worker, exec, framework, diag, logs, worktree, workspace — each selecting behaviour via an action argument.
Do not read controllers to guess at N+1s: route_timing, then dumps and profiler, then optimize_route joins the symptom to its cause with file:line.
Each worktree gets a <branch>.<site>.test subdomain; readiness must come from wait, never from inspecting the tree, because node_modules/ and vendor/ read as finished mid-install.
Curated version-specific rules plus the Boost MCP tools; search-docs before code changes because it returns docs matched to installed versions.
composer validate --strict, composer audit --locked, Pint, PHPStan with an explicit memory limit, coverage and Codecov upload on every push and pull request.

Both halves are checked rather than assumed from a green main run: packages must match their published releases, and the suite must pass against exactly those files. The tag pattern is v-prefixed because an unprefixed pattern matched none of this repository's tags and the workflow had never run.
One image driven by CONTAINER_MODE — http via Octane/RoadRunner, plus optional reverb and worker profiles — with MySQL, Redis and Mailpit behind health checks.
Turns bugs and feature requests into pull requests against main, checking rules such as unit tests for new business logic.
Composer, npm and github-actions ecosystems at the repository root.
Direct user-to-user messaging with encrypted bodies, read receipts and policy-based access, delivered as both a Blade/Alpine web UI and a Sanctum-authenticated REST API.
Holds sender/recipient relations, between()/unread() scopes and markAsRead()/isRead(); keeps conversation querying in one place rather than in controllers.
Seven actions (index, show, store, markAsRead, destroy, users, unreadCount) that validate input, authorize via policy and handle encryption/decryption at the boundary.

Laravel Policies chosen over ad-hoc checks: standard pattern, centralized logic, easy to test, and works with Blade directives and middleware. Users view messages they sent or received, update only what they sent, delete either side.
sender_id/recipient_id foreign keys with cascade delete, encrypted text body, nullable read_at.

Laravel Crypt (AES-256-CBC) encrypts each message body individually. Chosen because it is built in, needs no extra infrastructure, and manages keys via APP_KEY. Per-message rather than per-column encryption allows selective decryption and least privilege. Trade-offs: encrypted messages cannot be searched without decrypting, and key rotation requires re-encrypting everything.

Messages are stored directly and conversations derived dynamically: simpler schema, fewer joins, fast direct-message queries. Trade-off: adding group messaging would require refactoring to a conversations table plus a participants pivot.
Composite (sender_id, recipient_id) index optimizes the between() scope; a single recipient_id index optimizes unread-message queries used by the conversation list.
Keeps the web UI on session auth while exposing the same behaviour to token clients; enables future mobile app integration without reworking authentication.

Chosen over Vue/React because it is lightweight, needs no build step for the MVP, integrates with Blade and matches the Livewire ecosystem. Migration to Livewire components is noted as a future option.
Authorization is checked at routes (middleware), controller (policy) and views (Blade directives) so a single missed check cannot bypass access control.
Blade's @json() is used instead of raw {{ }} when embedding values into JavaScript, closing an XSS hole found in code review.
Seven endpoints: list conversations, conversation with user, send, mark read, delete, list users, unread count.
Blade views (layout/index/show) with a conversation list, unread counts and a new-message modal.
MessageTest covers model logic, relationships, scopes and encryption; MessageApiTest covers endpoints, authentication, authorization and validation.
Dual-channel delivery: every notification is persisted to the database for history and broadcast over websockets for immediacy, so reliability does not depend on the socket connection.
Ably, Laravel Reverb and Soketi are drop-in alternatives to Pusher, so the implementation avoids coupling to one vendor.
App.Models.User.{id}, user.{userId} and notifications.{userId} are all private and require channel authorization, keeping notification payloads off public channels.
All notifications implement ShouldQueue so broadcasting and persistence happen off the request cycle.
UUID primary key for distributed-system compatibility, polymorphic notifiable, JSON data column and read_at tracking.
Initializes only when Pusher env vars are present, subscribes to the authenticated user channel and re-dispatches a notification-received custom event for the UI to consume.
Service layer holding searchUsers/searchPosts/searchGroups/searchAll so filter-to-query translation is reusable and testable outside controllers.
Validates filters then delegates to SearchService; validation at the edge prevents malformed queries reaching the database.
/api/search/users, /posts, /groups and /all, each accepting query, entity filters, date ranges, ordering and per_page (1-100).
belongsTo author, with published/status/byAuthor/dateRange/search scopes.
belongsTo owner, with type/byOwner/search scopes.
scopeSearch on each model keeps search logic DRY and consistent instead of duplicating LIKE clauses in every controller.
B-tree indexes on searchable and filterable columns (name, title, status, created_at, is_active) plus foreign keys; expected 50-80% reduction in query time on indexed columns.
Groups carry a full-text index on name/description. Posts deliberately do not: they use plain B-tree indexes and LIKE matching via the search scope.
60 requests per minute per IP protects against DoS and enforces fair resource distribution.
Standalone search controllers select only needed columns (60-90% memory reduction). The shared SearchService does not yet do this and still returns full models.
Default 15, maximum 100 records per page prevents memory exhaustion from unbounded result sets.
The search code moved out of app/ into modules/search; the package README is the canonical reference.
Holds the demo-shaped Post and Group models that the search docs describe.
LIKE-based search suits small-to-medium datasets; Laravel Scout with Meilisearch/Algolia or Elasticsearch is the documented escape hatch for larger ones.
Modules are independently versioned Composer packages installed into modules/{name}; Composer owns discovery and autoloading.
Owns runtime metadata, provided/required capabilities, enablement defaults and Filament plugin declarations, separate from Composer's installation metadata.
Dependencies are declared twice on purpose: Composer require controls installation and autoloading, manifest requires/required_capabilities control the enabled runtime graph.
integration, domain, presentation or theme; framework presentation dependencies must stay out of domain packages.
Bundled packages default to disabled in their manifests and the application enables its composition explicitly, so installing a package never implies booting it.
The root application bootstraps only the module manager, which discovers installed liberu-module packages, validates the graph, orders providers by dependency and registers only enabled modules.
Runtime modules declare their provider in extra.liberu.provider and must not use Laravel's auto-discovery, because the module manager is the single provider lifecycle authority.

Checks that Liberu package dependencies are represented consistently, required versions are installed, providers are valid, capability providers are unambiguous and the enabled graph has no gaps or cycles.
A module must not query another module's tables or import its models as an integration API; use a contract, application service, event or documented schema extension instead.
Small shared-interface packages let adapters depend on a stable boundary without importing an implementation.
Filament code lives in a companion presentation package rather than its domain module, keeping domain packages presentation-agnostic.
The presentation manifest names which panel (admin or app) receives its plugin class; plugin identifiers must be unique within a panel.
Composes plugin instances from enabled manifests so panel providers never hard-code module plugins.
Panel key 'admin' is for operational management surfaces.
Panel key 'app' is for tenant/user-facing functionality.
Every module carries its own tests under modules/{name}/tests, at minimum metadata tests verifying Composer/manifest agreement, dependencies and the provider.
Hidden filesystem-scanning conventions are avoided so Composer metadata, the manifest and explicit enablement are enough to reproduce the composition.
Update the changelog, validate the graph, run focused and root suites, release from the package repository, then update the consuming application's constraint and lockfile.
Themes are independent Composer packages installed into tracked /themes/{name} directories and own presentation only; business rules, authorization, queries and mutations stay in modules.
Declares name, label, version, provider, type, parent, colors and the declared asset entries.
Child themes override only differing assets and inherit views/assets through a finite, validated parent chain; view lookup is child theme, parent chain, module default, then application fallback.
Shared root theme: accessible layout, semantic tokens, cascade layers and progressive JS primitives.
Dark presentation achieved purely through token overrides on base.
Composer 2 plugin handling both liberu-theme and liberu-module: validates kebab-case installer names, rejects unsafe paths and collisions, and installs deterministically to /themes or /modules.

Consuming applications commit both the lockfile and the reproduced /modules and /themes trees; root path repositories let Composer recognize the tracked source at the installer path instead of overwriting it.
Tenant-and-surface, then site-and-surface, then configured surface, then safe default. User/session preference may only select a discovered compatible theme; invalid selections warn and fall back.
Themes consume tokens for light, dark, contrast, state, focus, motion, spacing, typography, radius, elevation, borders, breakpoints and layering rather than hard-coded values.
WCAG 2.2 AA target verified with automated checks plus keyboard and screen-reader journeys; CSS honors reduced motion, forced colors and bidirectional layout; JS is progressive and CSP-safe.
Builds fail on missing manifest assets or unresolved imports; /public/build is deployment output while source assets remain in each package.
Discovers themes, resolves the active theme, exposes theme/view/asset paths and registers theme view paths with Laravel's view finder.
Registers the ThemeManager singleton, determines the active theme at boot, registers theme view paths and Blade directives, and shares theme data with views.
theme(), active_theme(), set_theme(), theme_asset(), theme_path(), theme_views_path(), theme_layout().
@themeCss, @themeJs, @themeAsset, @themeLayout and @themeVite; @themeVite selects declared built entries and falls back to the application bundle when unavailable.
Authenticated users persist to users.theme_preference; guests fall back to session storage.
vite.config.js reads every themes/*/theme.json and builds whatever assets.css and assets.js declare, so a consuming application needs no build change to add a theme.
Theme views, CSS and JS were consolidated from three split resources/ trees into one directory per theme, so a theme is added or removed as a single unit.

Release from the theme's own repository, update constraint and lockfile, reinstall, review the tracked /themes diff, validate, build and test. Conflicts are resolved by selecting a package version and reinstalling, never by hand-merging installed output; breaking manifest/token/slot changes need a major version.
English, Spanish, French and German out of the box, with automated machine translation and cached results.
Resolution order: locale query parameter, session value, authenticated user's preference, Accept-Language header, then the default locale.
Wraps the free MyMemory API; can be swapped by binding a subclass in a service provider, which keeps callers independent of the translation vendor.
API translations are cached for 30 days to stay within MyMemory's free-tier rate limits and avoid repeat calls.
Lives in modules/localization-livewire and is mounted where a switcher is wanted.
The localization code moved out of app/ into modules/localization, modules/localization-livewire and modules/localization-mymemory; each package README is canonical.
Basic Info / Roles & Permissions / Account Settings tabs reduce cognitive load on a long form; password is required on create and optional on edit.
Role multi-select, email verified, email unverified and recently-joined filters, with role and team count badges for fast visual scanning.
UserStatsOverview, LatestUsersWidget and UsersByRoleChart give an at-a-glance view of the user base.
Roles and permissions are managed through Shield on top of Spatie Permission, with team-scoped permissions; no new tables were needed.

One root CONTEXT.md glossary and one docs/adr/ directory cover the host plus every modules/ and themes/ package; switch to CONTEXT-MAP.md with per-package contexts only if module vocabularies actually diverge.
Output naming a domain concept must use the glossary's term; a missing term is a signal of either invented language or a real gap.
Output contradicting an existing ADR must surface the conflict explicitly rather than silently overriding it.
All issue and PRD operations go through the gh CLI, with the repo inferred from git remote.
Currently 'no'. GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare #42 must be resolved by trying gh pr view then gh issue view.
A single wayfinder:map issue holds Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog; child tickets are sub-issues, and blocking uses GitHub's native issue dependencies keyed on the blocker's numeric database id.
needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix — each label string equals its canonical role name in this repo.

The conformance deliverable: scope, every decision with its enforcement mechanism, the defect register, and the step -1 to 9 migration sequence with gates and rollback. Later step blocks correct earlier prose in the same document.
Closed at 15/15 tickets; its destination was a spec and no production code changed. A fresh effort means a fresh map, not reopening it.

The vendor was taken as liberu/* early then reversed by the owner back to liberusoftware/*. This puts the repo in deliberate disagreement with liberusoftware/documentation, which mandates liberu/* — a documentation PR is owed.
Shared test harness every package dev-requires; version 1.2.0 implements all seven boundary rules that were being kept in the host, making their deletion safe.
Idempotent fleet migration script, piloted on analytics-core and reverted, moved out of the scratchpad because WSL wipes /tmp on restart.

Nine packages 404 on Packagist, blocking the fleet migration because each package must resolve package-testbench standalone. The fallback is a per-package repositories vcs entry, which unblocks immediately at the cost of a later cleanup release wave.

vendor/composer/installed.json owns the autoload map and is written from each package's published composer.json, so a rename makes the host unbootable until the wave is published. The gate for a rename is each package's own suite, never the host's.

A root install reinstalls every package from Packagist over the tracked /modules and /themes files. git checkout alone does not recover it — untracked files the published packages brought in survive and can be committed as if they were real work.
Sweeping only changed packages let three stale packages and one regression reach GitHub; the whole fleet must be swept.

ModuleValidator compares each manifest against Composer\InstalledVersions, so a bumped manifest fails the boot until the package is published, tagged and composer update'd — expect a red host in between.
Composer resolves the tag, not main, so a stale tag is worse than no tag; bumping and re-tagging closed the gate.

ModuleBoundariesTest held 15 rules; seven moved to the testbench and the survivors are the whole-graph ones — theme parents resolving, Composer owning every autoload boundary, cross-package namespace dependencies, one Composer vendor, and the two enablement rules.
Three reusable workflows so every repository gets real CI without carrying a copy of the workflow body.
CLAUDE.md overrides the /handoff skill's temp-directory default because WSL wipes /tmp exactly when the next session needs the document.
0 of 48 packages declared config.allow-plugins, so composer update fails inside every package because pestphp/pest-plugin is blocked; --no-plugins is a measurement workaround, not the fix.

Several confident claims were wrong on inspection: a CI gate of --min=83 measuring 5.6%, twelve architecture rules of which two never worked, and 'standalone-testable' packages that could not install standalone.
The token was never shared or stored; it belongs in ~/.config/composer/auth.json or a GitHub Actions secret, never in a repo or a chat transcript.
Written so the next session does not re-derive state: it points at CONFORMANCE.md, the git log and CLAUDE.md rather than restating them, and records only environment state, traps and next steps.
Superseded by the step 5 handoff: its blocker is gone and its next-steps are done.

Tests move out of the host into the package that owns them; a test belongs in a package only if it needs nothing from the host. Moved so far: settings (3 tests), localization-core (locale middleware), localization-core-livewire (language switcher).
Its "Step N is done" blocks state what was actually found, including where the plan was wrong — the plan is corrected in writing rather than silently.
Shared boundary suites and test bootstrap so a new boundary rule is one testbench release rather than a 44-repository sweep. Version 1.7.0 at the time of this handoff.

34 packages shipped 1.2.0 with no tests/ at all; Pest aborts with 'The test directory [tests] does not exist'. The 44-package sweep passed only because the directory was still on disk locally. Fixed with a tracked tests/.gitkeep. Lesson: a fleet sweep does not prove what the tarball contains — only a reinstall does. Second occurrence of this class of error.
testbench 1.3.0 and 1.4.0 were tagged with a boundary suite that could not load. A tag is what Packagist publishes, so it is not recoverable the way a push is.
A package overriding defineEnvironment() without parent::defineEnvironment($app) loses the application key PackageTestCase sets (testbench 1.7.0).
ModuleValidator compares the manifest against InstalledVersions, so the window between the two is expected red, not a fault.
Sweep at -P 2 and retry; higher parallelism loses name resolution.

Moving SearchService::searchPosts()/searchGroups() and two search-api controller actions into search-demo is a three-package refactor, not a move: searchAll() aggregates over types, so the honest design is a searcher registry in `search` that `search-demo` registers into — which is exactly what CONFORMANCE §3.4 objected to being hardcoded. search's own tests follow the code, not the other way round.
Tests preserved at commit 33550079 need adopting into their own repositories.

ThemeManager* and ThemeSwitcherTest need installed themes, but discovery reads base_path('themes') rather than InstalledVersions the way ModuleDiscovery does, and Testbench's base path is its own skeleton. Fixing it also closes the theme-support §4 row, where three successive guards had to be loosened to make the package bootable.

Runs on liberusoftware/module-* queued over an hour; every suite passes locally with the same command CI runs, but nobody has seen the workflows themselves pass since the migration. Check before assuming.
Mutation-test a new rule; outward-facing steps get confirmed; the plan is corrected in writing when wrong; no Claude attribution footers.
Every module is an independently versioned Composer package of type liberu-module; hosts integrate through declared public boundaries rather than application-specific classes.

The trusted installer places each package under /modules/<installer-name>. The installed directory stays tracked by the host repository while Composer and its lock file remain the source of version truth.
Installing a package implies neither runtime enablement nor commercial entitlement; enablement is a separate explicit decision driven by the manifest's default_enabled.
Vulnerabilities go to security@liberusoftware.com with reproduction details and affected version, never through public GitHub issues, so the report can be handled privately.

Consumers grant only the permissions needed for exported capabilities and must not couple to internal tables or classes; authorization stays the host's responsibility unless a public authorizer contract is published.
The near-universal dependency of foundation modules — it discovers manifests and resolves enablement order.
A contract package lets analytics adapters stay independent of the core implementation and of each other.

Owns generic authorized activity timelines, mentions, subscriptions, internal comments, attachments and visibility controls as one versioned package. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Foundation\ActivityComments\ActivityCommentsServiceProvider, default_enabled no.

Writes each measured figure into the package's tests.yml, ratcheting only upward — a package that has lost coverage keeps its threshold and is reported rather than silently lowered.

Finds the highest level each package's src/ passes by bisection over a standalone resolution; levels are monotone, so four runs settle it instead of eleven.
Writes each measured level into tests.yml as the reusable workflow's phpstan-level input, ratcheting only upward and preserving the existing coverage-threshold.
